short_answer: If you want to view your GPX files, see your own activity heatmap or sketch a route to download, this free local tool may be enough. Strava offers a broader activity platform, including community features and route recommendations.
paywall: Strava lists personal heatmaps and route creation among its subscription features. See its personal heatmap guide and subscription feature list for current details.
free_does:
• Opens local GPX tracks and routes, with separate recording segments preserved.
  • Shows selected activities as lines and a heatmap of recorded point density.
  • Draws routes point by point, with draggable handles, undo, reverse and GPX download.
  • Works with an offline coordinate grid, plus optional OpenStreetMap street tiles.
  • Keeps files in tab memory, without accounts or uploads.
when_pay: Consider Strava if you want device syncing, a persistent activity library, social features, training analysis or suggested routes based on community activity. This tool joins manually chosen points with straight lines; it does not snap to roads or provide turn-by-turn navigation. Imports are limited to 20 files and 50,000 points in total, with 500 editable route points.
